items.title: 68099_Erskine Hawkins oral history interview
items.q: I remember Patrilla, one wire that they had out when recording was getting ready to start again. So, Patrilla sent everybody a wire to come to his office. I know I had to go to his office.

ctx.x: Yeah. Now, another significant thing that happened during the war years was the ban on records that they had, you know, partly because they couldn't, they would make an agreement with record companies and also because they were saving the shellac. You know, so they had this record, recording ban there. Did that affect you? Did you feel that?

Right because we couldn't record no more. I remember Patrilla, one wire that they had out when recording was getting ready to start again. So, Patrilla sent everybody a wire to come to his office. I know I had to go to his office. And, when I walked
through that door he said, If you do it, I'll throw you out of the union for the rest of your life."
